title: Surgical TTL & Keying Advisor for Cost-Sensitive Prefix Cache Policies
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Develop an automated advisor that proposes narrow, confidence-weighted TTL adjustments and keying tweaks for prefix/KV caches aimed at lowering per-token cost without degrading latency/quality. The advisor must combine an explainable hit-rate model, counterfactual simulation, and a staged apply/rollback orchestration that can be executed by Console or CI. This ticket covers model design, offline evaluation harness, UI suggestion payload, and a safe rollout blueprint (shadow, canary, automatic reversion triggers).
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces per-prefix TTL and keying suggestions with estimated cost delta and hit-rate confidence interval
Offline simulator demonstrates <5% median latency regression and >=3% expected cost reduction on historical traces for at least two customer cohorts
Console integration: suggestion appears in Policy Suggestions page with explanation text and one-click stage/rollback hooks
Automated rollout runbook enforces safety gates: absolute token cost cap, latency P95 SLO guardrail, and quality regression threshold (prompt eval metric)
Full rollback automation succeeds in synthetic chaos run (simulated traffic spike + cache eviction) within 10 minutes
notes: We intentionally avoid a global tuner: recommendations should be surgical and cohort-scoped (tenant, route, prefix-entropy bucket)
Model will use a two-stage architecture: (1) a probabilistic hit propensity estimator per prefix, (2) a survival-based TTL decay estimator to project hit-rate over time
Key-shaping rules focus on aggregating semantically identical prefixes and introducing soft-hashes to reduce cold-start duplication
Priority: start with read-heavy routes where caching dominates spend (embeddings & streaming decode prefixes)
We should surface uncertainty and show counterfactuals so operators can reason about risk vs reward
technical_design_summary: Estimator pipeline: ingest prefix-access traces -> feature extraction (recency, freq, burstiness, client-tenancy, seq-len distribution, response-churn) -> Bayesian hit propensity model (beta-binomial with hierarchical priors per-tenant) -> Weibull survival fit for TTL decay curves -> counterfactual simulator that replays traces with proposed config to compute token-level cost, cache hit/shadow misses, and latency implications. Output: ranked suggestion list with delta estimates and CI.
implementation_steps: Spike: build minimal hit-propensity estimator and local simulator using sampled trace (2d)
Feature engineering: add burst-detection, prefix-entropy, and batch-effect features (3d)
Estimator upgrade: add hierarchical priors and Thompson-sampling based uncertainty quantification (4d)
Simulator: integrate KV lookup cost model and batching interaction model; produce per-prefix counterfactuals (3d)
UI payload: draft suggestion schema and explanation text for Console team (2d)
Rollout harness: implement shadow canary, realtime SLO gating, and automated revert path (4d)
E2E test: synthetic traffic + chaos test for rollback timing and correctness (2d)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run on staging with synthetic prefixes and traffic to validate simulator outputs
Phase 1: Shadow-suggest against two pilot customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks, no live apply
Phase 2: Canary apply to 1% of traffic for pilot routes with latency and cost gating, 24h observation
Phase 3: Graduated ramp to 10% then 50% contingent on SLOs; automated hold if any gate trips
Phase 4: Full-enablement for cohort if sustained improvements and no regressions
rollback_plan: Automatic immediate revert if token-cost increases >7% or P95 latency increases >10% for 30m window
Manual escalation to on-call runtime engineer if revert fails or if anomalies persist after revert
Post-mortem template: include counterfactual snapshots, simulator inputs, and timeline of events
Fallback: pin TTLs to previous stable values and replay trace to compute difference for debugging
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Simulator mismatch with production workload due to batching interaction. Mitigation: include batching simulator component and validate against shadow-traffic logs
Risk: Key-shaping causes unintended cache collisions. Mitigation: conservative collision threshold, rollout in read-only shadow mode first
Risk: Operators distrust black-box suggestions. Mitigation: provide explainability (feature contribution) and CI for suggested change
Risk: Edge cases with long-tail prefixes. Mitigation: veto rules for prefixes under N accesses/day and default to conservative TTLs
customer_communication: Pilot customers will receive a one-pager describing advisor logic and opt-in instructions
Console will show predicted ROI and safety metadata for each suggestion
Help-center article draft: ‘How TTL suggestions work’ and ‘Interpreting advisor uncertainty’

Schedule 30m sync with Console PM and Ops for rollout gating decisions
Provision sampled trace export for first two pilot tenants
